status: Read-only proposal. No catalog, application, remote publication or permission/contact changes.
boundedScope: 20 active MIT source repositories examined: the ten with existing Openings README acknowledgment plus ten highest-volume remaining MIT sources. Inspected actual LICENSE and README contents and full returned LICENSE-path commit history (all under 100 commits). This is not an audit of every possible source, issue attachment, separate agreement or historical GitHub Terms version.

recommendedProvisionalSet.name: 16 issue-board sources with explicit README MIT notice
recommendedProvisionalSet.status: Documented repository-license basis for review, not universal legal certification or proof of individual employer authorization.

documentaryBasis.summary: GitHub D.6 says content added to a repository containing a license notice is licensed on those terms, subject to a separate agreement. D.5 is limited to GitHub-service functionality and is not unrestricted external permission. D.3 retains ownership and requires authority over posted material.
documentaryBasis.reasoning: For these issue-based vacancy repositories, the actual MIT notice plus README licensing language and preexisting license history provide a specific basis to evaluate issue contributions under D.6. This is more evidence than an API license label or public accessibility. README acknowledgment of Openings is supporting context, not the grant.
documentaryBasis.historicalFinding: For all 20 reviewed sources, the latest LICENSE-file change predates the earliest currently indexed issue. Most histories contain one license commit. This establishes notice chronology, not authorship/title clearance or complete historic-contract verification.
documentaryBasis.mitCondition: MIT permission is conditional on preserving its copyright and permission notices in copies or substantial portions. Source links alone should not be represented as fulfillment of the license notice condition. Actual mobile/web/data notice preservation was not verified by this task.

proofLimits: No source-specific blanket grant by every employer/issue author to Openings was found or invented. If the chosen threshold is signed/express individual permission only, this evidence set does not meet that threshold.

Repository MIT wording uses software and associated documentation. GitHub D.6 and issue-board README context are the proposed bridge to issue contributions; the file alone is not conclusive for all third-party content.

Some licenses retain frontendbr/Android Dev BR copyright boilerplate from forks. Preserve the actual notice; do not replace its named holder with Openings or assume the maintainer owns each employer description.

Current READMEs/LICENSEs did not reveal a job-content carve-out in the recommended set. All .github templates, private agreements, historical Terms versions and individual attachments were not exhaustively examined.
Employer content, logos/avatars, trademarks, contributor authority and privacy interests remain separately assessable; no broad rights certification is claimed.

Historical source API records or external detail pages must not remain accessible merely because the visible list is filtered. If the user selects restriction, root should decide the operational scope and notices before making compliance claims.

deferred.reason: Actual MIT files and issue-board purpose verified, but no explicit README MIT notice. They add 37 unique jobs to the 16-source shortlist. Not declared forbidden; held out of the first-pass recommendation for a clearer documentary packet.

CC0 files or README notices exist in prior audit, but wording sometimes identifies this text/copied README, and Rebase mentions its own distribution channels. Do not automatically treat all author job descriptions as public-domain; scope needs a separate bounded review.
No broad applicable content reuse license established in inspected materials. Public posting or encouraging derived projects is not represented as universal authorization.
README states ingestion from external job platforms, adding an upstream-content-rights gap.
Already removed for non-job issues. Explicit README exclusion of job postings from MIT demonstrates why repository code license metadata cannot be used blindly.

implementationIfRootApproves: Restrict ingestion to approved source shards before normalization/deduplication, then rebuild public artifacts. Do not filter already merged canonical records by one allowed source while retaining disallowed descriptions/metadata.
Preserve exact source copyright and permission notices in distributed copies using a source-license register/notice mechanism; confirm reviewer-accessible presentation.
Keep source links, contributor attribution and correction/removal channel, without framing them as substitutes for permission.
Review old detail artifacts, cached/public snapshots and pending output separately; no external deletions or republishing occurred in this task.
Recheck new sources and document license scope/time before ingestion; hold changes when there is an explicit content exclusion or incompatible notice.

safeReviewClaim: The proposed restricted catalog contains issue-based vacancy repositories with documented MIT notices and source README licensing language. We rely on those notices together with GitHub's contributions-under-repository-license terms, preserve required notices, and retain source links. We do not characterize public GitHub content as public domain or assert endorsement by every employer.
safeReviewClaimCondition: Only use after the source restriction and required notice preservation actually exist and root verifies them. Before implementation, describe it as a proposal.
calculation: Executed existing buildStaticApiFiles in memory on only allowed repository shards. No snapshot files were written. Asserted each retained primary record and all its source entries belonged to the selected set.
